title: 藏经阁残简 第三章 苛利刁难暗蓄锋芒藏经阁残简 第四章 残卷纳身灵气复涌
slug: 残简道藏我靠修复古籍证道
content_zh:
藏书阁外，脚步声粗重拖沓。
刘松一袭灰衣管事袍，面色不耐，负手立在廊下，目光扫过阁内整齐陈列的书卷，半点没有赞许，只剩惯常的刻薄与挑剔。
他执掌西阁多年，素来欺软怕硬。
沈砚道基破碎、沦为废杂役的三年里，他克扣月例、肆意使唤，早已成了常态。尤其沈砚曾是宗门天才，落得这般境地，在刘松这种小人物眼里，更是绝佳的拿捏对象。
“磨蹭什么？”
刘松见沈砚缓步走出，眉头当即一竖，语气尖锐，“让你整理的名册迟迟不交，整日躲在阁里偷懒。若非宗门规矩，你这种废人，连守书的资格都没有！”
沈砚神色平静，不起波澜。
三年来这般冷言苛责，他早已听惯。
若是从前，他唯有隐忍退让，低声应答。可此刻神魂深处流淌着淡淡的文道暖意，丹田道基虽未完全修复，却已然有了复苏迹象。
他眼底沉静如故，只是心底那三年积压的委屈与压抑，早已悄悄松动。
“名册已整理完毕。”
沈砚抬手，递出一卷装订整齐的纸质册页。
字迹工整，条理清晰，所有残简、朽卷、破损玉简皆分门别类，标注清楚，比往年任何一次都要规整周全。
刘松随意接过，扫了两眼，没挑出错处，心中微恼，却又找不到苛责由头，便转而寻别的事端。
他目光一斜，瞥向阁楼深处堆积的废弃残简，冷声道：
“近日宗门清点库存，这批朽烂旧卷，尽数定为废籍，明日统一焚销毁掉。你今日之内，全数分拣出来，搬到后院废书坪堆放。”
此言一出，沈砚眸光微凝。
那些看似毫无价值的残简朽卷，恰恰是整座西阁最珍贵的宝藏。
旁人眼中是无用垃圾，于他而言，每一卷都是可修复的道藏、可补道基的机缘。
若是尽数焚毁，万千失传文脉、无数古法道韵，将彻底化为飞灰。

更甚者，这是他目前唯一的修行根基。
沈砚抬眼，声音依旧清淡：“此批残简虽破损严重，但仍有文字遗存，贸然焚毁，恐有损宗门文脉留存。”
“文脉？”
刘松像是听到天大的笑话，嗤笑一声，居高临下睨着沈砚，满眼讥讽，“一个道基崩碎、终生无望修行的废人，也配谈文脉？宗门正统道书无数，还差这点破烂废纸？”
“我告诉你沈砚，安分做事，少多嘴。”
“今日天黑之前，分拣不完，本月灵石，尽数扣除。”
话音落下，他狠狠将名册往沈砚手中一塞，转身拂袖而去，不留半分余地。
克扣灵石，是刘松拿捏他最惯用的手段。
沈砚三年无半点额外资源，全靠每月微薄灵石勉强吊住灵气，一旦月例被扣，连最基础的修行维系都难。
换做往日，他只能咬牙强忍，日夜操劳补工。
可此刻，沈砚握着名册，立在光影浮沉的藏书阁中，脊背挺直，眼底掠过一抹极淡的冷光。
扣他灵石？
无妨。
从今往后，他早已不需要仰人鼻息，靠这点微薄月例修行。
万千残简在手，便是他无尽道源、无尽资源。
“要焚我机缘……”
沈砚低声轻语，声音极轻，却带着前所未有的笃定。
他不会允许。
content_en:
Outside the library, footsteps were heavy and shuffling.
Liu Song was dressed in a gray steward's robe, with an impatient look on his face. He stood in the corridor with his hands behind his hands. His eyes scanned the books neatly displayed in the pavilion. There was no approval at all, only his usual meanness and pickiness.
He has been in charge of the West Pavilion for many years and has always bullied the weak and feared the strong.
In the three years since Shen Yandaoji was broken and reduced to a useless handyman, it has become the norm for him to deduct the monthly routine and do whatever he wants. In particular, Shen Yan was once a genius of the sect, and ended up in this situation. In the eyes of a little person like Liu Song, he was an excellent candidate for manipulation.
"What are you dawdling about?"
When Liu Song saw Shen Yan slowly walking out, his brows immediately stood up and he said in a sharp tone, "I asked you to delay submitting the roster you compiled and hide in the pavilion all day long. If it weren't for the sect's rules, a loser like you wouldn't even be qualified to keep the book!"
Shen Yan's expression was calm and unruffled.
He was already used to hearing such cold words and harsh words in the past three years.
In the past, he could only hold back and respond in a low voice. But at this moment, there is a faint warmth of literature and art flowing deep in the soul. Although the Dantian Daoji has not been completely repaired, there are already signs of recovery.
His eyes were as calm as ever, but the three years of accumulated grievances and depression in his heart had long been quietly loosened.
"The roster has been compiled."
Shen Yan raised his hand and handed out a neatly bound paper album.
The handwriting is neat and organized, and all broken slips, rotten scrolls, and damaged jade slips are classified into categories and clearly marked, making them more organized and thorough than ever before.
Liu Song took it casually, glanced at it, and didn't find anything wrong. He was slightly annoyed, but he couldn't find a reason to blame him, so he turned to look for other troubles.
He glanced sideways at the abandoned scraps piled deep in the attic, and said coldly:
"Recently, the sect has taken inventory. These rotten old books have all been classified as waste books and will be burned and destroyed tomorrow. You will sort them out today and move them to the waste book pile in the backyard for stacking."
As soon as these words came out, Shen Yan's eyes narrowed slightly.
Those seemingly worthless scraps and decaying scrolls are precisely the most precious treasures in the entire West Pavilion.
In the eyes of others, they are useless garbage, but to him, every volume is a repairable Taoist treasure and an opportunity to mend the Taoist foundation.
If they are all burned, thousands of lost cultural contexts and countless ancient dharma and Taoism will be completely turned into ashes.
What's more, this is the only foundation for his current practice.
Shen Yan raised his eyes, his voice still calm: "Although this batch of scraps is seriously damaged, there are still written remains. Burning them hastily may damage the preservation of the sect's cultural heritage."
"Context?"
Liu Song seemed to have heard a big joke and sneered. He looked down at Shen Yan with sarcasm in his eyes, "A useless person whose Taoist foundation is broken and has no hope of practicing for the rest of his life is worthy of talking about cultural background? There are countless orthodox Taoist books in the sect, and what is left of this tattered piece of paper?"
"I'm telling you Shen Yan, do your work calmly and talk less."
"The sorting will not be completed before dark today. All the spiritual stones for this month will be deducted."
As soon as he finished speaking, he thrust the roster into Shen Yan's hands, turned around and walked away without leaving any room.
Stealing spiritual stones was Liu Song's most common method of controlling him.
Shen Yan has had no extra resources for three years, relying solely on the meager monthly spiritual stones to maintain his spiritual energy. Once the monthly routine is deducted, it will be difficult to maintain even the most basic practice.
In the past, he could only grit his teeth and endure it, working day and night to make up for the work.
But at this moment, Shen Yan was holding the roster, standing in the library with floating light and shadow, his back straight, and a very faint cold light flashed across his eyes.
Deduct his spiritual stone?
No problem.
From now on, he no longer needs to rely on others to practice his cultivation on this meager monthly routine.
Having thousands of broken bamboo slips in his hand is his endless source of truth and endless resources.
"If you want to burn my opportunity..."
Shen Yan whispered in a low voice, his voice was extremely soft, but with unprecedented certainty.
He won't allow it.
